# core/utf8.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/utf8.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

UTF-8 validation (RFC 3629). A sequence is valid when
it is one of the shortest encodings of a Unicode scalar value: no
overlong forms, no surrogates (U+D800 to U+DFFF) and nothing above
U+10FFFF.

What is proved: no read is out of bounds, a sequence length is 0 (invalid)
or 1 to 4 and stays inside the string, and a count never exceeds the
number of bytes. Not proved: that the accepted sequences are exactly the
ones RFC 3629 lists (the tests check the boundary cases of each form).

`import "core/utf8.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`utf8_seq_len`](#utf8_seq_len) | The length of the valid UTF-8 sequence that starts at byte `i`, or 0 if the bytes at `i` are not a valid sequence (a stray continuation byte, an overlong form, a surrogate, a value above U+10FFFF, or a sequence cut short by the end of the string). |
| [`utf8_valid`](#utf8_valid) | `b` is valid UTF-8 (the empty string is). |
| [`utf8_count`](#utf8_count) | The number of characters (Unicode scalar values) in `b`, or `None` if `b` is not valid UTF-8. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `utf8_seq_len`

```bastio
fn utf8_seq_len(b: &Bytes, i: u64) -> u64
  requires i < blen(b)
  ensures result <= 4 && i + result <= blen(b)
```

The length of the valid UTF-8 sequence that starts at byte `i`, or 0 if
the bytes at `i` are not a valid sequence (a stray continuation byte,
an overlong form, a surrogate, a value above U+10FFFF, or a sequence
cut short by the end of the string).

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("aé€😀");
let one = utf8_seq_len(b, 0);     // 'a'
let two = utf8_seq_len(b, 1);     // U+00E9
let three = utf8_seq_len(b, 3);   // U+20AC
let four = utf8_seq_len(b, 6);    // U+1F600
let mut cut = balloc(2);          // a 3-byte lead cut short
bset(&mut cut, 0, 226);
bset(&mut cut, 1, 130);
let bad = utf8_seq_len(cut, 0);
bfree(cut);
bfree(b);
if one != 1 || two != 2 || three != 3 || four != 4 || bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `utf8_valid`

```bastio
fn utf8_valid(b: &Bytes) -> bool
```

`b` is valid UTF-8 (the empty string is).

Example:

```bastio
let ok = bfrom("café €");
let mut over = balloc(2);        // C0 80: an overlong NUL
bset(&mut over, 0, 192);
bset(&mut over, 1, 128);
let mut sur = balloc(3);         // ED A0 80: a surrogate
bset(&mut sur, 0, 237);
bset(&mut sur, 1, 160);
bset(&mut sur, 2, 128);
let good = utf8_valid(ok);
let bad = utf8_valid(over) || utf8_valid(sur);
bfree(ok);
bfree(over);
bfree(sur);
if !good || bad { return 1; }
```

### `utf8_count`

```bastio
fn utf8_count(b: &Bytes) -> Option[u64]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some <= blen(b)
```

The number of characters (Unicode scalar values) in `b`, or `None` if
`b` is not valid UTF-8.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("aé€");
let mut bad = balloc(2);         // 'a' then FF, which no sequence uses
bset(&mut bad, 0, 97);
bset(&mut bad, 1, 255);
let mut n = 0;
match utf8_count(b) { Option::Some(x) => { n = x; }, Option::None => {} }
let none = utf8_count(bad);
let rejected = none is Option::None;
match none { Option::Some(x) => {}, Option::None => {} }
bfree(b);
bfree(bad);
if n != 3 || !rejected { return 1; }
```

### `utf8_cont`

```bastio
fn utf8_cont(c: u8) -> bool
```

Internal: `c` is a continuation byte, `80`..`BF`.
